item.title: Digital Technologies for Combating Unethical Labour Practices and Promoting Human Rights
item.content:encoded:
Stefan Gold, Technical University of Munich

Antoine Harfouche, Paris Nanterre University

Paul Jones, Swansea University

Maryam Lotfi, Cardiff University

Guoqing Zhao, Swansea University

An estimated 50 million people worldwide experience unethical labour practices, with numbers expected to rise due to regional conflicts and restrictive migration policies. While digital technologies such as blockchain, AI, and cloud computing offer potential solutions for monitoring and addressing these practices, research in this area remains limited. This special issue seeks to understand how digital technologies can theoretically and empirically be deployed to monitor, detect, report, and remediate unethical labour practices.

The special issue welcomes original research using various methodologies that examines the relationship between digital technologies and unethical labour practices. Submissions should identify specific technologies examined and move beyond surface-level analysis to provide nuanced insights. The collection particularly encourages studies that challenge existing paradigms, explore underexamined aspects, or propose innovative frameworks for leveraging digital solutions to advance ethical and sustainable societies while informing policymakers, business leaders, and practitioners.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Role of digital technologies (blockchain, AI, cloud computing, IoT, big data analytics, virtual and augmented reality) in monitoring and detecting unethical labour practices
  • Application of digital technologies to address modern slavery, human trafficking, forced labour, and other forms of labour exploitation
  • Digital technologies for reporting and remediating unethical labour practices in supply chains
  • Use of machine learning and AI for identifying trafficking patterns and at-risk populations
  • Blockchain applications for tracking labour exploitation in global supply chains
  • Digital technologies for social inclusion and reintegration of survivors of modern slavery
  • Biometric recognition and satellite imagery applications by governments and NGOs
  • Comparative analysis of multiple digital technologies versus single-technology approaches
  • Theoretical frameworks and conceptual models for understanding digital technology adoption in addressing unethical labour practices
  • Empirical studies on the effectiveness and limitations of digital solutions in combating labour exploitation

Timeline

  • February 15, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Unpacking Digitalization: Antecedents, Strategies, and Performance Implications
item.content:encoded:
Jasmina Berbegal-Mirabent, Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya

Angelo Cavallo, Politecnico di Milano

Antje Fiedler, University of Auckland

Esteban Lafuente, Instituto Tecnológico de Costa Rica

Digital technologies are fundamentally reshaping how both private and public organizations—including universities, hospitals, and local administrations—conceive strategy, innovate, and compete. However, scholarly understanding remains fragmented regarding how digitalization operates across different functional areas and organizational levels, and literature has not fully clarified the mechanisms through which technological adoption generates performance gains or the conditions under which it falters.

Appel publié par Review of Managerial Science. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Antecedents of digital technologies adoption: Strategic approaches including organizational, technological, institutional, and market-related factors influencing SMEs' digitalization strategies
  • Differences in digitalization strategies between industries or economic contexts
  • Strategic choices and prerequisites supporting digitally-induced organizational actions
  • Socio-technical system readiness factors including technical infrastructure, organizational culture, workforce capabilities, and data governance maturity
  • Ecosystem characteristics and their role in shaping digitally enabled interactions
  • Human-technology interaction and integration of digital technologies into firm operations
  • Value-adding strategies promoted through digital technology integration
  • Organizational resources, processes, and competencies supporting digital technology integration
  • Strategic purposes for technology integration: automation, augmentation, cybersecurity, and innovation
  • Digital literacy, ethical concerns, organizational culture, and managerial practices in technology adoption
  • Digital transformation in the public sector with constrained resources
  • Leadership, governance structures, and resource orchestration in public institutions
  • E-administration, hybrid learning platforms, and AI-enabled service delivery in public organizations
  • Spillover effects of public digital initiatives on regional SMEs
  • Public-private partnerships and cross-sector collaborations for digital solutions
  • Governance models and knowledge-sharing mechanisms enhancing digital co-creation
  • Absorptive capacity development through partnerships
  • Sector and regional ecosystem factors affecting partnership effectiveness
  • Performance outcomes of digital technologies and technology-enabled strategies
  • Individual-level outcomes including productivity, learning, creativity, and decision quality
  • Firm-level outcomes including innovation, internationalization, operational efficiency, and sustainability
  • Mechanisms explaining heterogeneous digitalization outcomes across individuals, teams, and firms
  • Digital literacy and human-technology interactions shaping performance outcomes
  • Strategic alignment of competencies and digital technologies for competitive advantage
  • Digital transformation impacts on power dynamics between entrants and incumbents

item.title: Managing the digitally-savvy workforce: Human Resource Management in an evolving digital landscape
item.content:encoded:
Sanjay Singh, University of Dundee

Sateesh Shet, Northumbria University

Tanya Bondarouk, The University of Twente

Paresha Sinha, University of Waikato

James Duggan, Cork University Business School

The acceleration of digital transformation across industries has reshaped the nature of work and the workforce. In this evolving landscape, a new kind of employee has emerged, one that is digitally fluent, technology-enabled, and increasingly reliant on digital tools to perform, collaborate, and innovate. This digitally-savvy workforce brings with it a unique set of expectations, behaviors, and capabilities that are fundamentally altering traditional models of Human Resource Management.

As organizations navigate this shift, HRM must move beyond conventional practices to align with the realities of a workforce deeply embedded in digital ecosystems. The integration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, virtual collaboration platforms, and HR analytics is not only transforming operational HR functions but also reshaping strategic priorities around talent acquisition, workforce planning, performance management, employee engagement, and learning and development.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Human Resource Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Strategic workforce planning for the digital era, including forecasting digital talent needs, digital upskilling frameworks, and bridging digital skills gaps
  • Work design for digitally enabled workforce, encompassing job roles in technology-mediated environments, digital flexibility, autonomy, work-life integration, and remote work impacts
  • Emerging digital technologies and HRM transformation, including AI, blockchain, virtual reality, chatbots, intelligent automation, and HR digital twins
  • Redefining talent acquisition for digitally-savvy workforce through social media recruitment, gamified assessments, AI in recruitment, and employer branding
  • Performance management in tech-driven organizations, covering digital dashboards, algorithmic evaluation, surveillance, real-time feedback, and fairness implications
  • Employee engagement and experience in digital workspaces, including digital platforms, AI-driven personalization, digital fatigue, and tech-enabled burnout
  • Ethics, privacy, and surveillance in digital workplace, addressing algorithmic monitoring, employee autonomy, and ethical HR technology adoption
  • Inclusion, equity, and accessibility in digital HR practices, focusing on digital exclusion reduction, neurodiverse talent support, and fair AI-driven decision-making

  • August 1, 2026: Manuscript submission window opens
  • September 30, 2026: Manuscript submission deadline

item.title: Neurophysiological Foundations and Effects of Contemporary Digital Technologies
item.content:encoded:
René Riedl, University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria & Johannes Kepler University Linz

Jan vom Brocke, University of Münster

Jella Pfeiffer, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology

Robert Gleasure, Copenhagen Business School

The advent of increasingly powerful artificial intelligence systems (e.g., large language models such as ChatGPT, diffusion models, graph neural networks, or vision transformers used in healthcare, manufacturing, software development or finance), together with other contemporary digital technologies (e.g., autonomous cars, immersive worlds, and neuroadaptive interfaces), has fundamentally reshaped human interaction with information systems. As these technologies become embedded in work, consumption, private life, and society in general, the ways in which they affect human cognition, emotion, and social interaction remain poorly understood.

Appel publié par European Journal of Information Systems. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How does sustained interaction with AI-enabled systems (e.g., LLMs) and other advanced digital tools reshape neural networks associated with language, reasoning, and memory?
  • Does reliance on AI systems and other forms of automation/digital decision support alter attentional control, working memory, metacognition, or problem-solving processes at the neurophysiological and behavioral levels?
  • What are the implications of digitally augmented cognition for neuroplasticity, skill acquisition, and expertise development over time?
  • How can integrated neurophysiological and behavioral measures provide a fuller picture of technology-mediated cognitive processes?
  • How do individuals' brains respond to empathetic or anthropomorphic cues exhibited by conversational AI and other interactive systems?
  • What neurophysiological correlates underlie trust, reliance, distrust, or skepticism toward AI systems and other algorithmic or platform-based systems?
  • How does emotional regulation change when decision-making is mediated by AI support, algorithmic decision aids, or digital nudges?
  • What are the neurophysiological mechanisms of stress, fatigue, or overload in contexts of AI-assisted work and other digitally intensified work settings?
  • How does technological mediation in team collaboration influence the neurophysiological foundations of social coordination, empathy, and shared attention?
  • What neural mechanisms underlie shifts in authority, leadership, and influence when AI becomes a co-decision-maker?
  • How do cultural differences modulate neurophysiological responses to AI and other digitally mediated collaboration settings?
  • How do gender, age, or personality differences modulate neurophysiological responses to IS artifacts?
  • How might AI-driven systems and other algorithmic/persuasive designs reinforce or mitigate cognitive biases?
  • What neural signatures accompany ethical dilemmas and moral decision-making in AI-mediated contexts and broader digital governance settings?
  • How does long-term use of AI and other digitally intensive work systems shape neurophysiological well-being, stress, or mental health at the workplace?
  • How can neurophysiological insights inform the design of AI systems and other digital systems that are more intuitive and aligned with human cognitive limits?
  • What are the neurophysiological underpinnings of productivity, efficiency, or value creation in digitally mediated economic interactions?
  • How can genetic and neurophysiological approaches together explain individual differences in the adoption and use of digital systems?
  • Which neurophysiological tools are best suited for investigating contemporary IS phenomena?
  • How can hybrid approaches combining neurophysiology with computational methods enrich IS theory development?
  • How can multi-level research designs integrate genetic, neurophysiological, behavioral, self-report, and organizational data to address IS phenomena more holistically?

Timeline
